reviews.title: $80 for 10 Minutes of Use. A $20 Annual Plan Was Available. Buyer Beware.
reviews.text:
This app’s subscription pricing is absurd, and my experience has left me with absolutely zero trust in how they do business.

I signed up for a free trial, opened the app maybe twice, and used it for approximately 10 minutes TOTAL. I forgot to cancel before the trial expired. That’s my mistake, and I fully acknowledge it.

But then I was charged $80 for an annual subscription. I caught it the same day and immediately requested a cancellation and refund.

Denied.

Then I discovered something even more ridiculous. Hidden among the subscription options in my settings were multiple annual pricing tiers, including $20, $80, and options reaching $150. For the same app. With no obvious explanation for the enormous price differences.

Why was I charged $80 when a $20 annual option was available? What exactly justifies charging one customer FOUR TIMES as much? How is anyone supposed to make an informed purchasing decision with pricing this inconsistent?

I offered a completely reasonable compromise: refund the $60 difference and let me keep the $20 annual subscription. I wasn’t even asking for a free year.

Denied. Again.

So here’s the situation: I used this app for roughly 10 minutes, was charged $80, requested a refund the SAME DAY, discovered I could apparently have paid $20 for an annual subscription, and couldn’t even get the price difference refunded.

reviews.title: Great concept, but completely breaks down on cable exercises due to pulley physics blind spot
reviews.text: While this app is a fantastic tool for tracking standard barbell and dumbbell movements, its strength ranking system (Bronze, Gold, Platinum, etc.) completely falls apart on cable machines because the algorithm is blind to mechanical pulley ratios.Currently, the app assumes that 1kg entered into the log equals 1kg of actual force on the muscles. In the real world of commercial gym equipment, this is false:Raw Weight vs. Effective Resistance: On an unadjusted machine with a standard 2:1 pulley ratio (like a Matrix multi-gym), selecting 73kg on the weight stack means the pulleys cut the load in half. The user is only lifting an effective resistance of 36.5kg of true force, but they log "73kg" in the app.Adjusted True-Weight Labels: On a high-end functional trainer with a 4:1 ratio (like a Life Fitness Signature DAP), the manufacturer explicitly states that the label indicates the true resistance at the handle. To deliver 40kg of actual tension, the machine moves 160kg of physical iron plates. The user logs "40kg" in the app because that is what the plate says.Because there is no option in the app to input the machine's pulley ratio, your database is fundamentally flawed. A user pulling a true, brutal 40kg of unassisted resistance on a Life Fitness machine is unfairly low-balled into a "Bronze" tier. reviews.title: Billed $80 with no “reminder” to cancel as offered by the app
reviews.text:
I’ve seen a lot of the 1-star reviews on here relate to how the app gives u a free trial, and asks if you want to be reminded to cancel it in advance. I had the same situation where I was trying out the app, and saw an $80 payment go through. No cancelation reminder. The same day I requested to cancel it, providing valid reasons and prompt cancelation time. I have never had an issue with the Apple store providing a refund from more reputable apps, especially if it has only been ~1 day and I haven’t used the app or the subscription benefits. 

Don’t advertise notifying about canceling the subscription before the trial ends if you aren’t going to. I normally set my own personal reminders and this influenced me to just rely on the app. Thanks.

reviews.title: Buggy + lack of supported exercises
reviews.text:
At first it looked like a good app and one of its best features was its design. It was comparable to Duolingo.

However, it was a buggy mess. The app wouldn't necessarily freeze, but it would prevent me pressing certain buttons unless I exited out of the app. I restarted the app probably a dozen times until i gave up.
In addition, i found it hard to navigate. I just wanted to track my PRs, but it forced me to track my whole workout, which i didnt want to do.
The app also forced me to get a free subscription. I couldnt opt out of it. I mean, It sounds good, but If i didnt manually cancel this subscription, i would have to pay $80 once the trial ends.

The app is also only good for powerlifting, not for general athleticism. I dont want to just track my deadlift or bench press- I want to be able to track my 2 mile runs or 800m intervals, but in this app, it isnt possible.
They also dont account for the fact that the weights on the machines could be different. For example, i could do 130 lb pec flies in one gym and then 180 at the one at planet fitness.
Also, many exercises do not have the ability to give your rank. This is fine, but at least LET me track my PR for the exercise. For example, the plank. I have a 6min plank that i am rly proud of, but I cant even enter my plank time in this app.

Thats about it for this rant. Ill give a 2 star since the design of the app looks nice (even though its hard to navigate)

reviews.title: Cool concept, but recent update broke it. No customer support.
reviews.text:
I initially bought the annual subscription after enjoying the brief trial period and really liking how the workout builder and rest timer kept me accountable during my lifts. I also liked the ease of using the calorie tracker, however during their most recent update the calorie tracker is now completely broken and assuming impossible caloric burns even before you’ve logged anything to the day. For example: I go to the nutrition tab and it says I have 8000+ calories remaining for the day I can consume because I have already burned 7000+ calories, despite having logged nothin for the day. 

I’ve emailed the app developers twice since the update and there’s been no response. I feel like I’ve sunk $90 into an app that essentially lost its most central purpose. 

There are plenty of other apps out there that probably have better customer support.
